jobs.title: Sr. Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About PrologMobile
Nobody in the global reverse supply chain for mobile devices knows exactly what they are buying or selling. PrologMobile fixes that. We are a device intelligence company: give us an IMEI or serial number, and our platform returns essential data points about that specific device, including carrier and SIM lock status, blocklist and financial risk, Find My iPhone and MDM locks, warranty, and whether it will work on a given carrier network.
Carriers and MVNOs, insurers, device processors, ITADs, marketplaces, and wholesalers build our data into their trade-in, resale, and claims workflows. Our customers use it to cut returns, prevent fraud, and price devices accurately.
A few things that make us different:
Founders who lived the problem. Our founders have spent more than 20 years in the secondary device market and helped start the mobile device recycling industry in North America.
Real technical moats. We hold a US patent (11,711,755 B1) and co-developed the Device Compatibility service with the GSMA. We are active in CTIA and the GSA.
Work that matters. Every device that gets resold instead of scrapped stays out of a landfill. Our data touches the lifecycle of tens of millions of devices a year.
A small team. We are about a dozen people. There is no layer between you and the decision, the customer, or production.
Our mission is to be the most trusted, most comprehensive device intelligence platform in the world.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks
jobs.description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
How it works
Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.
Requirements
2+ years of professional software engineering
Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
Regular use of an AI coding tool
Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
At least 10 hours a week, starting now
A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)
Nice to have
Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
Experience building agent tasks or RL environments
Terms
US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork
Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

Join iA – Transforming Pharmacy Fulfillment with Innovation and Care
Are you ready to revolutionize pharmacy with cutting-edge automation technology? At iA® (Innovation Associates®), we are at the forefront of transforming how pharmacies manage prescription fulfillment. With over 30 years of experience and innovation, iA is advancing pharmacy automation with solutions such as the NEXiA® Enterprise Software Suite, enabling pharmacists to focus more on patient care while improving operational efficiency. We’re looking for passionate and driven individuals like YOU to help shape the future of healthcare. Join us and be part of a team that's changing the way pharmacy works—for the better.
Your Role & Its Purpose:
NEXiA is the software that runs pharmacy fulfillment hardware (counting machines, collation systems, and conveyor routing) in pharmacies across North America. It has been in production for years and has moved from Access to VB6 to VB.NET, and it now runs as a 32-bit [.NET Framework] application. It was built to solve real problems and still does, but its architecture wasn’t redesigned along the way.
You’ll improve it from the inside while shipping real features. There’s no multi-year rewrite on the table; progress comes through daily work. Some days you’ll build a new feature in clean C#. Other days you’ll make a legacy VB.NET module testable so it can be extended or eventually replaced. You’ll make judgment calls about what to fix now, what to isolate, and what to leave alone, within the direction set by the engineers leading our DDD-based decomposition.
We expect AI agents to be a core part of how you work: pointing them at undocumented modules, generating characterization tests, proposing migration paths, and running multi-step refactors. You review everything, because in a codebase with no documentation these tools produce plausible but wrong descriptions of behavior.
If you’re effective in legacy codebases, this is work you can see: your code runs physical equipment in real pharmacies, on a small team. If you’ve only worked on greenfield projects or need a modern stack to be productive, it’s probably not the right fit.

Platform Engineering & Feature Delivery
Build and ship features across the NEXiA platform — pharmacy workflows, hardware integration, operator interfaces — working within and improving the existing codebase
Own features end-to-end: understand the domain context, design the approach, implement across the legacy/modern boundary, test, and support through deployment
Work across the full stack — VB.NET backend, .NET Core services where they exist, front-end interfaces, SQL Server data access, and hardware integration layers
Write code that moves the codebase forward: when you touch a module, leave it more testable, more maintainable, and closer to modern patterns than you found it
Legacy Code Improvement & Migration
Navigate and improve a VB.NET codebase that has evolved through multiple technology generations without architectural rethinking
Identify opportunities to migrate legacy components to modern .NET/C# — not as a separate initiative, but as part of feature delivery and defect resolution
Build and maintain the seams between legacy VB.NET code and modern .NET components; manage the coexistence practically
Apply pragmatic judgment about what to modernize now versus what to isolate and defer — not everything needs to be rewritten, but nothing should be left unexaminable
Quality & Testing
Write meaningful tests for code that was never designed to be testable — introduce test seams, extract interfaces, break dependencies as needed
Build automated validation that works across the legacy/modern boundary, catching regressions before they reach customer environments

About the Role
Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand.
We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents.
This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation.

Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts.
Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.
Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards.

Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content.

High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes.
Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap.
Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones.
